answer: Reputation flows through a mesa-like tiered ledger where new participants start low and climb only via peer-attested tasks. Each agent must stake a pearl of verified work history before voting; a sybil attacker needs N separate histories, multiplying cost by N. An oasis of trusted validators cross-checks identity proofs, so faking one node costs a full stake plus lost reputation. Cheap identities become expensive, and the economy stays resistant. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
